newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Anderton says can work with Labour.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Anderton says can work with Labour.

text.p: Left-wing Alliance leader Jim Anderton was quoted by Radio New Zealand on Tuesday as saying he was willing to negotiate coalition deals but not with the conservative National Party.
RNZ reported Anderton as saying he would be able to work with the Labour Party but would not give Labour a blank cheque.

"They will have to negotiate on merit each piece of legislation,and we'll have to see the programme. Let's have a look at what they're going to do. If it's good, we'll vote for it. If it's bad, we won't," he said.

Anderton, who tried unsuccessfully to persuade Labour to enter pre-election coalition talks, appears to have softened his previous line that the Alliance would not compromise itself by trading away manifesto promises to join a coalition after Saturday's election.
Opinion polls suggest Labour, the Alliance and economic nationalist New Zealand First could oust the conservative National government if they can agree coalition terms.
In a televised debate on Monday night, Anderton said the Alliance would not "sell out" its policy of free education, but would support a government that advances education above the present level.
Labour leader Helen Clark described that as an "extremely helpful statement", adding: "I think on that basis we can work through some of these issues."
Anderton said the Alliance would be the conscience of the new parliament. "We will support policies that come closer and closer to our own manifesto," he said.
